traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Heracleum lanatum: stems 1 m to 3 m tall. The typical value is the one the plant was drawn at before, inside the source's range.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a giant herb with hollow stems, huge maple-like leaves of three lobed leaflets and broad, flat umbrellas of white flowers. Not fitted to measurements. basal_area is the area its `basal` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), 0.299 since its trifoliolate leaf sets its lateral pair at the petiole's tip (was 0.212).

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 2 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves; white umbels.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: Jepson eFlora's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): rays 15 to 30, 5 to 10 cm, unequal. The Flora of North America gives 15 to 35 (40), its umbels 15 to 30 cm wide.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its compound umbel drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c): its kind from the carrot family's inflorescence and its rays from its own, by the rules at the flowering plants; about 20 flowers in each umbellet (Illinois Wildflowers gives 8 to 30; no flora gives a count), each about 6 mm across with five white notched petals, on pedicels 1 to 2 cm long (Jepson: 8 to 20 mm), the umbel about 25 cm across (the Flora of North America: 15 to 30 cm). From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. The enlarged outer flowers are not drawn. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white notched petals with no sepals (by hand: sepals obsolete, Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, 1951, read in full) on the inferior ovary, five stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Apiaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Heracleum lanatum, p. 239, fig. 3605: leaves 2 to 5 dm long, round to kidney-shaped in outline.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: leaves ternately compound once, the three leaflets lobed in various ways but not divided again.

traits.leaflets.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: leaves ternately compound, that is of three leaflets (divisions), each coarsely serrate and lobed in various ways.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: ternately compound, so one of the three leaflets ends the rachis.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: leaf divisions 15 to 40 cm long (the scan's OCR reads '15^0 cm'; read as 15-40, which agrees with general accounts of leaflets up to 40 cm).

traits.inflorescence_bracts.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: involucre bracts 5 to 10, lanceolate with a drawn-out tip, falling early (the genus line says the involucre is usually absent: in this species it is present but deciduous). No bract length given. Peduncles densely villous under the umbel.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), Heracleum, p. 239: flowers usually white (genus line; the species account adds nothing). RGB for 'white', slightly warm.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: fruit obovate to obcordate, 8 to 12 mm long, hairy, strongly flattened on the back with broad thin lateral wings (genus).

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as H. lanatum, p. 239: flowering February to June over its whole range (Alaska to California).

traits.fruiting_months.note: Restoring Western Ranges and Wildlands, vol. 2 (Monsen and others 2004, ch. 19, p. 441, read 2026-10-16), as Heracleum lanatum in the Intermountain West: flowers "bloom in July and early August. Seed matures in late August and early September"; read as August and September. The Range Plant Handbook (1937) says the fruits "usually ripen during September"; FEIS (Esser 1995) gives flowering only.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: Each leaf ternate (Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, vol. 3, 1951, as Heracleum lanatum): three broad, coarsely toothed and lobed leaflets, the end one on a longer stalk; drawn as a compound card of three leaflets about as wide as long, their lobes not drawn. Its kind and leaflet count from the species' characters by the rules at the flowering plants; the leaflets' width, teeth, stalks and angle by eye.

appearance.organs.basal.note: Its basal leaves as its stem leaves (Abrams 1951: ternate, the leaflets broad and lobed), on longer petioles, by eye.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
